requirement:
Saved execution-coverage checks select the most recent recorded attempt
for each nextest binary and test name within the instrumented configuration
of the most recently started recorded attempt. Most recent refers to when an
attempt started, including failed or interrupted attempts. A newer filtered
run updates only tests it executes, leaving other compatible records available.
A newer attempt with missing or unreadable coverage is unavailable and does
not fall back to an older success. Incompatible configurations under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.configuration` are excluded.
Selection uses recorded metadata without building or executing tests.
rationale:
I judged this from the supplied test sources and did not request implementation source. The reviewed tests cover every obligation in `requirements.test-coverage.index.selection`.

- **Latest attempt per binary and test name.**
  - `selection_distinguishes_binaries_and_selects_latest_attempts_within_the_active_build` has two cases. It records the same test name under two binaries and asserts that both binaries are selected. It also writes several attempts for the same test and asserts that the newest is chosen.
  - A further case puts a retry in the same run, with attempt start deliberately contradicting UUID and file order. The assertion expects the later-started attempt's count of 1.
  - `history_selection_loads_measurements_only_for_latest_attempts` records three attempts for `one`. It asserts that only the latest is selected and that the older ones keep metadata without measurements.
- **Most recent means attempt start, not run start.**
  - In `selection_distinguishes_binaries_and_selects_latest_attempts_within_the_active_build`, run start and run ID ordering deliberately disagree with attempt-start ordering. The build-b run is given start 1000 while its attempt starts at 35. The assertion that the selected tests are `{one, two}` therefore only holds when selection follows attempt start.
- **Configuration of the most recently started attempt.**
  - The same test selects the build-a records because the newest attempt (`two` at 40) is build-a. The build-b attempt is excluded even though its run started later.
  - `filtered_runs_union_latest_attempts_and_invalidate_with_saved_source` records a newer build-b attempt and asserts that exactly one record is selected and that its configuration is build-b. This covers exclusion of incompatible configurations under the cited `storage.configuration`.
- **Filtered runs update only the tests they execute.**
  - `filtered_runs_union_latest_attempts_and_invalidate_with_saved_source` records `one` and `two` in separate runs and asserts that both are selected. It asserts that the union has counts for lines 1 and 2.
  - `history_selection_loads_measurements_only_for_latest_attempts` also checks that the newer `two` attempt leaves the `one` attempt selected.
- **Newer failed, interrupted, missing or unreadable attempts do not fall back to an older success.**
  - `filtered_runs_union_latest_attempts_and_invalidate_with_saved_source` adds a newer attempt with outcome `failed` or `interrupted` and a missing-profile diagnostic. It asserts that the check does not pass and that its text contains "missing or unreadable coverage".
  - `unreadable_history_cannot_reintroduce_an_older_success` covers four failure forms: invalid metadata, missing source, unsupported schema and a missing profile file. It asserts that the check fails and that no positive older-success counts leak through.
  - `malformed_historical_measurements_make_selection_uncertain` covers malformed measurement data. It asserts that `uncertain_history` is set and that the selection stays as the latest attempt.
  - `selected_attempt_cannot_be_replaced_between_selection_and_loading` checks that measurements fail to load if the selected attempt changed after selection.
- **Selection uses recorded metadata without building or executing tests.**
  - `book_rendering_preserves_retained_coverage_and_never_launches_tests` in `tests/execution_coverage.rs` runs `coverage-check` and the mdbook preprocessor with a `cargo` wrapper that fails on any command other than `metadata`. It asserts that no forbidden command ran, that the test-execution marker file was not created, and that the stored files are unchanged.
  - The metadata-cache tests, `metadata_cache_preserves_selection_and_detects_edits_with_restored_mtime` and `a_corrupt_optional_metadata_cache_does_not_hide_saved_measurements`, check that selection from recorded metadata stays correct when the cache is stale or corrupt.

I found no obligation without a test that asserts its outcome, and no marking gap. Ties in start time are not specified by the text, so I did not treat them as a gap.
